meta.name: Firstmate skill map
meta.tagline: Lanes, skills and guards of the supervisor, in the order one task meets them. Click any box. Upstream skills are described from their own docs; this site did not run each one. Dashed boxes are planned.

labels.stageNote: **This is a step, not a skill.** The boxes inside it are the skills, lanes and guards a task meets here.
labels.anyNote: **Not tied to one step.** These are shared references, or lanes that are planned and not built.

stages.name: Intake
stages.principle: Find out **what** the task is and **where** it belongs.
when: When the owner gives a new ask → you are in Intake
When a session starts or restarts → you are in Intake

stages.name: Instruct
stages.principle: **Write it down**, then start one worker in its own copy.
when: When the ask is clear → you are in Instruct

stages.name: Run
stages.principle: The worker **works**. The supervisor **waits** without spending tokens.
when: When a worker has its brief → you are in Run

stages.name: Check
stages.principle: **Read the real state.** Do not take the worker's word.
when: When a worker reports done → you are in Check

stages.name: Land
when: When a pull request is ready → you are in Land

stages.name: Learn
stages.principle: Keep what was learned. The **next** Intake reads it.
when: When the task is closed → you are in Learn
stages.gap: The nightly rule proposals have not been seen to run.

categories.name: Start of a session
categories.principle: A new session first **reads the state on disk**. It does not trust its memory.
when: When the start-up digest shows unfinished checks → session-start-recovery
When it shows a set-up problem → bootstrap-diagnostics
categories.chainWhy: Each one loads only when the digest prints its trigger. They do not run in a fixed order.

categories.name: Take the ask
categories.principle: Sort the ask into a **project** and a **mode**: find facts (scout) or change code (ship).
when: When a project must be added or removed → project-management
When the ask is a bug report → diagnostic-reasoning
categories.chainWhy: Two separate jobs. Which one applies depends on the ask.

categories.name: Pick up where you left off
categories.principle: Show the owner what **waits on them** before anything new starts.
when: When the owner asks for a status digest → bearings
When the owner asks for a recap of visible events → ahoy
categories.chainWhy: Both are typed by the owner. Neither calls the other.

categories.name: Choose who does it
categories.principle: When more than one agent profile could take the task, **pick by rule**.
when: When a dispatch rule gives more than one candidate → quota-array-dispatch

categories.name: Brief and start
categories.principle: A worker gets **written instructions** and nothing else. Then it starts.
when: When the ask is clear → task-brief
When the brief is written → harness-adapters
categories.chainWhy: The brief comes first. The start step reads it.

categories.name: Guard: own copy
categories.principle: A worker **never** edits the owner's main copy.
when: When any worker starts → isolated-copy

categories.name: Scout lane
categories.principle: A scout **finds facts** and writes a report. It pushes nothing.
when: When the task is to investigate → scout

categories.name: Ship lane
categories.principle: A ship **changes code** and ends in a pull request. The owner says when it merges.
when: When the task is to change code → ship

categories.name: Second mate lane
categories.principle: A second mate is **persistent** and optional. It runs from its own home.
when: When the owner opts in to a persistent helper → second-mate
When its home must be set up or retired → secondmate-provisioning
categories.chainWhy: Set up the home before you rely on the mate.

categories.name: Watch the crew
categories.principle: A shell watcher waits on the status files. It **wakes the supervisor** only when something needs it.
when: When a worker looks stuck → stuck-crewmate-recovery
When a long-polling source must be armed → process-event-sources
categories.chainWhy: Both are triggers on a wake. They do not follow each other.

categories.name: While the owner is away
categories.principle: Change how often the supervisor wakes the owner.
when: When the owner types /afk → afk
When the owner types /quiet → quiet

categories.name: Guard: safety hooks
categories.principle: A hook is a script the tool **must** run. It turns a rule into a check.
when: When a worker runs a shell command → safety-hooks

categories.name: Scout reports
categories.principle: A report is not complete while the owner still owes a decision.
when: When a scout reports completion → scout-completion
When an owner question is still open → hold-lifecycle
categories.chainWhy: Check the report first. Then check that no question waits.

categories.name: Guard: plain English
categories.principle: A **program** checks the report. The scout does not grade itself.
when: When a scout is about to say done → plain-english-check

categories.name: Ship gate
categories.principle: A pre-push gate **validates** the change. A finding that asks the owner goes to the owner.
when: When a ship has a validation run → validation-supervision
When a finding asks the owner → ask-user-authority
categories.chainWhy: The run produces findings. The policy says who answers them.

categories.name: Land the work
categories.principle: Register the pull request, **watch it**, tell the owner.
when: When a ship reports a pull request → ship-landing

categories.name: Guards: land
categories.principle: Real state first. The owner's word second. Clean-up only after landing.
when: When a pull request is registered → live-merge-check
When it is ready → owners-word
When the owner has merged → landed-work-check
categories.chainWhy: Each check needs the one before it.

categories.name: The learning loop
categories.principle: A note becomes a **proposal**. The owner **reviews** it. Only then it becomes a rule.
when: When a session ends → session-notes
When notes pile up → rule-proposals
When a proposal is ready → owner-review
categories.chainWhy: No step skips the owner. The instruction files are what the next Intake reads, so the loop closes.

categories.name: Keep it current
categories.principle: Save durable facts. Update the supervisor.
when: When the owner types /stow → stow
When the owner types /updatefirstmate → updatefirstmate

anytime.name: Planned lanes (not built)
anytime.blurb: Five lanes that are written down. None is built or proven.

session-start-recovery.name: session-start-recovery
when: When the start-up digest reports ==unfinished checks== or output that needs reading → [[session-start-recovery]]
session-start-recovery.whatItIs: An **upstream** skill. It tells a new session how to read the start-up digest and recover.
howItWorks: The session starts and prints a digest
A line shows unfinished checks or a recovery input
The skill loads and says what to do with it

bootstrap-diagnostics.name: bootstrap-diagnostics
when: When the start-up digest prints an ==actionable diagnostic line== such as a missing tool → [[bootstrap-diagnostics]]
A silent section means the skill does not load
bootstrap-diagnostics.whatItIs: An **upstream** skill. It explains each diagnostic line the start-up check can print.

project-management.name: project-management
when: Before the supervisor ==adds, creates, removes or initializes== a project → [[project-management]]
Cloning or registering a project counts as adding
project-management.whatItIs: An **upstream** skill. It holds the steps for project intake, so the supervisor does not guess them.

diagnostic-reasoning.name: diagnostic-reasoning
when: Before scoping a ==reported bug== → [[diagnostic-reasoning]]
Before acting on a diagnostic report → [[diagnostic-reasoning]]
diagnostic-reasoning.whatItIs: An **upstream** skill. It sets how the supervisor reasons about a fault before it starts work.

bearings.name: bearings
when: When the owner asks ==where they left off== or what is in the works → [[bearings]]
bearings.whatItIs:
An **upstream** skill. It builds a digest of the supervisor's own state: what waits on the owner, what runs, what is next.

**Status: not proven.** It was not run for this site.

ahoy.name: ahoy
when: When the owner types ==/ahoy== → [[ahoy]]
ahoy.whatItIs: An **upstream** skill. It recaps visible session events and guides the owner through decisions nobody has answered yet.

quota-array-dispatch.name: quota-array-dispatch
when: When a dispatch rule gives ==more than one profile candidate== → [[quota-array-dispatch]]
quota-array-dispatch.whatItIs: An **upstream** skill. It decides which agent profile takes the task when a rule names several.

task-brief.name: task-brief
when: When the ask is clear and a worker will do it → [[task-brief]]
task-brief.whatItIs: Every task starts as a **written brief**: the intent, the spec, the rules and a definition of done. A worker does one task and nothing outside the brief.
howItWorks: Spec: where to write and what to build
Rules: never push, one status line per phase change, ask before an owner decision
Done: what evidence ends the task

harness-adapters.name: harness-adapters
when: Before the supervisor ==spawns or recovers== a worker → [[harness-adapters]]
Before it sends a tool-specific command, handles a trust dialog or exits an agent → [[harness-adapters]]
harness-adapters.whatItIs: An **upstream** skill. It holds what differs between agent tools when a worker is started, resumed or stopped.

isolated-copy.name: isolated-copy
when: Every time a worker starts → [[isolated-copy]]
isolated-copy.whatItIs:
**A guard.** Each worker gets its own git worktree and its own status file. It works in that copy, not in the owner's main one.

Upstream runs each worker as a normal agent session in a visible terminal window. It does not use a tool's built-in sub-agents.

**Evidence:** this site was built by one such worker.

scout.name: scout
when: When the task is to ==investigate or audit== → [[scout]]
scout.whatItIs: **A lane, not a skill.** A scout finds facts. Its output is a written report. It pushes nothing. Its worktree is thrown away after.

ship.name: ship
when: When the task is to ==change code== → [[ship]]
ship.whatItIs: **A lane, not a skill.** A ship changes code. Its output is a pull request or a local merge. The owner says when it merges.

second-mate.name: second-mate
when: When the owner opts in to a ==persistent helper== that keeps its own queue → [[second-mate]]
second-mate.whatItIs:
**A lane, not a skill.** Upstream describes an optional second mate: an ordinary direct report that runs from its own isolated home, on this machine or on another host.

**Status: not proven.** This site reports no run of one.

secondmate-provisioning.name: secondmate-provisioning
secondmate-provisioning.trigger: set up or retire a mate's home
when: When a second mate's home is ==created, launched, recovered or retired== → [[secondmate-provisioning]]
secondmate-provisioning.whatItIs: An **upstream** skill. It holds the steps for a second mate's home, from seeding to retirement.

stuck-crewmate-recovery.name: stuck-crewmate-recovery
when: When a worker's window is dead, loops, or ==does not answer== → [[stuck-crewmate-recovery]]
stuck-crewmate-recovery.whatItIs: An **upstream** skill. It tells the supervisor how to find out why a worker stopped and how to steer it.

process-event-sources.name: process-event-sources
when: Before the supervisor ==arms a long-polling source== or registers a condition-to-action watch → [[process-event-sources]]
process-event-sources.whatItIs: An **upstream** skill. It covers sources that raise a wake when a set condition becomes true.

afk.name: afk
when: When the owner types ==/afk== or says they are away → [[afk]]
afk.whatItIs: An **upstream** skill. The supervisor takes an away posture and shows a return brief when the owner is back.

quiet.name: quiet
when: When the owner types ==/quiet== and stays in the session → [[quiet]]
quiet.whatItIs: An **upstream** skill. It cuts routine wake turns while the owner is present. Unlike /afk, ordinary chat does not end it. Only `/quiet off` does.

safety-hooks.name: safety-hooks
safety-hooks.trigger: block a command before it runs
when: Before a worker's shell command runs → [[safety-hooks]]
safety-hooks.whatItIs:
**A guard.** A hook is a script the tool must run. Three parts:

1. **Directory change.** Upstream's cd-guard stops a command that changes directory in an unsafe way (docs/cd-guard.md). **Designed upstream.**
2. **Shell file writes.** The owner's hook blocks heredoc-to-file, tee and sed -i. It blocked commands in a worker's own session. **Working.**
3. **Secret prints.** The owner's hook blocks a command that would print a secret. **Installed. Not triggered in a recorded test.**

scout-completion.name: scout-completion
when: When a scout ==reports completion==, shows a visual for iteration, or may be promoted to a ship → [[scout-completion]]
scout-completion.whatItIs: An **upstream** skill. It sets what the supervisor does before it treats a scout's work as finished.

hold-lifecycle.name: hold-lifecycle
when: Before a report is ==treated as complete==, and when the owner's answer is recorded → [[hold-lifecycle]]
hold-lifecycle.whatItIs: An **upstream** skill (see docs/captain-hold-lifecycle.md). An owner decision is a task that waits for the owner. A worker does not close a task while such a question is open.

plain-english-check.name: plain-english-check
when: Before a scout says ==done== → [[plain-english-check]]
plain-english-check.whatItIs:
**A guard, and the owner's own addition** to a private fork. It is not upstream.

A small program checks the scout's report for Simplified Technical English (STE100-style) rules. It flags long sentences and vague words. The scout does not grade itself.

**Evidence:** commit f33019a6 (2026-10-28). It makes one test fail on purpose (T6). See Testing in public.

validation-supervision.name: validation-supervision
when: When a ship starts or has an ==active validation run== → [[validation-supervision]]
Before the supervisor answers any finding from the run → [[validation-supervision]]
validation-supervision.whatItIs:
An **upstream** skill. A pre-push gate (no-mistakes) validates the change before it goes out. The supervisor watches that run.

**Status: designed, not proven.** The full ship path with the gate was not run for this site.

ask-user-authority.name: ask-user-authority
when: Before the supervisor ==decides any ask-user finding== → [[ask-user-authority]]
ask-user-authority.whatItIs: An **upstream** skill. It is the single owner of the policy for findings that ask the user.

ship-landing.name: ship-landing
when: When a ship ==reports a pull request== or ready branch → [[ship-landing]]
While landing is watched, and before clean-up → [[ship-landing]]
ship-landing.whatItIs: An **upstream** skill. It runs the landing of a ship's work. A worker's ready signal must name a head that is pushed, not one that exists only in its disposable copy. The supervisor then registers the pull request and tells the owner the full URL.

live-merge-check.name: live-merge-check
live-merge-check.trigger: ask the forge, not the worker
when: Once a pull request is ready → [[live-merge-check]]
live-merge-check.whatItIs: **A guard.** A script registers the pull request and its head commit, and arms a merge poll. The state comes from the forge. It does not come from the worker's message. A draft pull request is refused. A ready signal whose commit is not pushed is blocked.

owners-word.name: owners-word
when: Before anything is ==merged, sent, published or spent== → [[owners-word]]
owners-word.whatItIs: **A guard. The owner decides here.** Only the owner holds the level that merges. The worker opens the pull request and stops. Upstream says an owner instruction to merge is explicit authority.

landed-work-check.name: landed-work-check
when: Before a task's copy is ==torn down== → [[landed-work-check]]
landed-work-check.whatItIs: **A guard.** The supervisor tears down a ship's copy only after landing is confirmed. If the teardown refuses because of uncommitted or unlanded work, that is a stop-and-look result. Nobody forces it without the owner's say.

session-notes.name: session-notes
when: When the owner says ==end of session== → [[session-notes]]
session-notes.whatItIs: A hook reminds the agent to write a short session note: goals, decisions, and where the agent went its own way. **Installed.** It works in one tool only, on the exact words.

rule-proposals.name: rule-proposals
when: Each night, over the session notes → [[rule-proposals]]
rule-proposals.whatItIs:
A tool (backpass) reads the notes and **proposes** edits to the instruction files. It never writes them.

**Status: installed. The nightly job was not yet seen to succeed** (as of 2026-10-31).

owner-review.name: owner-review
when: Each morning, for every proposal → [[owner-review]]
owner-review.whatItIs: **The owner decides here.** The owner reads each proposal and applies it or not. Facts enter long-term memory only after review.

instruction-files.name: instruction-files
when: At the start of every session → [[instruction-files]]
instruction-files.whatItIs: One plain-text rules file that every agent reads, plus per-project files. A reviewed rule lands here. **This closes the loop:** the next task's Intake starts from these files.

stow.name: stow
when: When the owner types ==/stow==, or before a context reset → [[stow]]
stow.whatItIs:
An **upstream** skill. It sweeps the session for durable knowledge and files it.

**Status: designed, not proven.** Nothing starts it before auto-compaction. It was not exercised recently.

updatefirstmate.name: updatefirstmate
when: When the owner types ==/updatefirstmate== → [[updatefirstmate]]
updatefirstmate.whatItIs: An **upstream** skill. It updates a running Firstmate and its second mates to the latest source.

agent-skill-trigger-index.name: agent-skill-trigger-index
when: When the trigger index itself is ==audited or maintained== → [[agent-skill-trigger-index]]
agent-skill-trigger-index.whatItIs: An **upstream** skill that is only a table: each agent-only skill and the exact event that must load it.

operational-home-layout.name: operational-home-layout
operational-home-layout.trigger: find a config or state path
when: When a home, config, data or state path must be ==located or changed== → [[operational-home-layout]]
operational-home-layout.whatItIs: An **upstream** skill. It says where Firstmate keeps its home, config, data, state and project folders.

comms.name: comms
when: **Planned.** Not built.
comms.whatItIs: **Planned lane. Not built. Nothing here is proven.** It would handle text and calls. Each message or call goes out only with the owner's word.

mail-and-calendar.name: mail-and-calendar
when: **Planned.** Not built.
mail-and-calendar.whatItIs: **Planned lane. Not built. Nothing here is proven.** It would plan the day from mail and calendar, voice first. It proposes. The owner decides.

home.name: home
when: **Planned.** Not built.
home.whatItIs: **Planned lane. Not built. Nothing here is proven.** It would help with groceries, house help and stock. Nothing is ordered or booked without the owner's word.

content.name: content
when: **Planned.** Not built.
content.whatItIs: **Planned lane. Not built. Nothing here is proven.** It would run a pipeline for short video and writing. It drafts. Nothing is published without the owner's word.

markets.name: markets
when: **Planned.** Not built.
markets.whatItIs: **Planned lane. Not built. Nothing here is proven.** It would score trade setups for a human, who places every trade.
